source_text: Primo illud scire debemus, quod aliud est de deo sentire, quod ingenitus sit et sine ullo initio, aliud de unigenito filio eius... (Rufinus I.2 lead; OCR apparatus omitted in tip).
pass_a_gloss: First we must know that it is one thing to think of God as unbegotten and without any beginning, another to think of his only-begotten Son.
pass_b_english: After the Father, we treat the Son: he is the [[Wisdom of God >> Bible:1 Corinthians 1:24]], the [[Word who was with God >> Bible:John 1:1]], image of the invisible God, not a creature among creatures. The Holy Spirit is joined in the apostolic preaching with the Father and the Son; Scripture assigns him unique works of sanctification, and he is not to be ranked among the made things.
notes: Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
